    Publications

    Journal Articles

    Smartphone-based multi-contrast microscope using color-multiplexed illumination

    Published in Scientific REPORTS, 2017

    A smartphone-based portable microscope enabling single-shot bright-field, dark-field, and differential phase contrast imaging of transparent specimens. Multi-contrast imaging is achieved using a patterned color micro-LED array and a color image sensor. A custom smartphone module and Android app perform image acquisition, computation, and real-time display.

    Recommended citation: Jung, D., Choi, JH., Kim, S. et al. Smartphone-based multi-contrast microscope using color-multiplexed illumination. Sci Rep 7, 7564 (2017)

    Single-exposure quantitative phase imaging in color-coded LED microscopy

    Published in OPTICS EXPRESS, 2017

    A single-shot quantitative phase imaging method using a color-coded LED microscope (cLEDscope). Red, green, and blue LEDs illuminate the sample at different angles, and phase reconstruction is achieved through computation with a color image sensor. A correction scheme is introduced to address color leakage from non-ideal LED and sensor spectra, improving phase accuracy.

    Recommended citation: Wonchan Lee, Daeseong Jung, Suho Ryu, and Chulmin Joo, "Single-exposure quantitative phase imaging in color-coded LED microscopy," Opt. Express 25, 8398-8411 (2017)

    Color-coded LED microscopy for multi-contrast and quantitative phase-gradient imaging

    Published in BIOMEDICAL OPTICS EXPRESS, 2015

    A multi-contrast microscopy method using color-coded LED illumination and computation. Bright-field, dark-field, and differential phase contrast (DPC) images are simultaneously obtained from a single color image. Quantitative phase imaging is achieved using DPC images acquired under two illumination patterns.

    Recommended citation: Donghak Lee, Suho Ryu, Uihan Kim, Daeseong Jung, and Chulmin Joo, "Color-coded LED microscopy for multi-contrast and quantitative phase-gradient imaging," Biomed. Opt. Express 6, 4912-4922 (2015)
